channel.title: Language Lineage
channel.description: Guides and data stories on what programming languages are written in, how compilers are bootstrapped, and how languages influenced each other.

item.title: How Modern Languages Trace Their Toolchains Back to C | Language Lineage
item.description: How Python, Rust, Go, JavaScript, Java, Ruby, and Haskell trace their compiler or runtime implementation back to C or C++. 7 chains computed from the Language Lineage dataset.

item.title: GraalVM vs HotSpot: Two JVM Implementations Compared | Language Lineage
item.description: HotSpot (C and C++) is the standard JVM in OpenJDK. GraalVM replaces the C2 JIT with a Java-written compiler and adds polyglot and Native Image support. Both run the same bytecode.

item.title: TypeScript vs JavaScript Compilers: tsc, swc, esbuild | Language Lineage
item.description: TypeScript adds types to JavaScript. The official compiler tsc is self-hosting TypeScript; swc is written in Rust; esbuild is written in Go. All three transpile to JavaScript.

item.title: V8 vs SpiderMonkey vs JavaScriptCore | Language Lineage
item.description: All three major JavaScript engines are written in C++. V8 powers Chrome and Node.js, SpiderMonkey powers Firefox, and JavaScriptCore powers Safari.

item.title: How Are Programming Languages Made? | Language Lineage
item.description: Learn how programming languages are designed and implemented. Languages are built using other languages, compilers and interpreters are programs written in existing languages.

item.title: GCC vs LLVM: Compiler Infrastructure | Language Lineage
item.description: GCC and LLVM are the two dominant open-source compiler infrastructures. Both are written in C++. Learn how they differ and which languages use each.

item.title: How Rust is Bootstrapped | Language Lineage
item.description: Rust is a self-hosting language. The Rust compiler (rustc) is written in Rust itself. Learn how the Rust bootstrap process works.

item.title: How Python is Implemented | Language Lineage
item.description: CPython is the reference Python implementation, written in C. PyPy uses RPython. Learn how Python interpreters work and what language each is written in.

item.title: How JavaScript Engines Work | Language Lineage
item.description: JavaScript engines like V8, SpiderMonkey, and JavaScriptCore are written in C++. Learn how they parse, compile, and execute JavaScript code.

item.title: Programming Language Family Tree | Language Lineage
item.description: The programming language family tree: how Fortran, LISP, and C influenced and implemented the languages that followed, across 75+ years of compiler and runtime history.

item.title: Compiler vs Interpreter vs Runtime | Language Lineage
item.description: Understand the difference between a compiler, interpreter, and runtime, and how these determine what language an implementation is written in.

item.title: What is a Self-Hosting Compiler? | Language Lineage
item.description: A self-hosting compiler is a compiler that can compile its own source code. Learn which languages are self-hosting and why it matters.

item.title: What is Compiler Bootstrapping? | Language Lineage
item.description: Compiler bootstrapping is the process of writing a compiler for a language in that same language. Learn how it works and which languages use it.

item.title: The Most Influential Programming Languages | Language Lineage
item.description: Reverse PageRank over 252 cited influence relationships across 131 languages. Generated, not hand-ranked.
